title: One installation, one active authenticated customer
method: Regressions written and observed RED before the production change (10 of 11 failing), then GREEN; a route case added as the wiring landed. Six sabotage reversions.

measured_before.already_closed: The takeover was closed earlier in this audit: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means an install is claimed once, so a stranger who guessed an install id could no longer re-attribute a victim's acquisition source.
measured_before.still_wrong_1: identifyInstall ended `customerId: String(link?.customer_id ?? customerId)`. When a SECOND customer verified their own phone on that device, the call returned the FIRST customer's id to them. A caller that trusts that value has been handed somebody else's identity by an install string - precisely what 'the installation identifier must never be treated as proof of customer identity' forbids.
measured_before.still_wrong_2: There was no release. A genuinely reset or resold device could never be re-bound, so its new owner stayed permanently unlinked - and DO NOTHING gave them no signal that anything had failed.
measured_before.still_wrong_3: Neither the claim nor the refusal was recorded anywhere, so a contested device left no trail at all.

approved_rules_implemented.one_active_context: install_identity_links carries the single active binding, with additive status/released_at/released_reason columns. Nullable and defaulted, so every row written before this reads back as the active binding it was.
approved_rules_implemented.no_silent_transfer: A claim on a held install is refused, audited as claim_refused, and the caller is handed THEIR OWN id - never the holder's.
approved_rules_implemented.handover_is_two_steps: releaseInstall then identifyInstall, which is the logout-then-login the rule describes. Deliberately not a single call: a transfer nobody signed out of IS the silent transfer.
approved_rules_implemented.release_authority: Only the current holder may release their own binding, and only with a stated reason. A staff release passes actorId so it is recorded as one rather than disguised as the customer's own action.
approved_rules_implemented.audit: install_identity_events records every claim, refusal and release, each carrying the account it replaced - a single mutable row cannot record an old-and-new linkage, it only ever knows the present.
approved_rules_implemented.session_is_authoritative: identifyInstall refuses without an authenticated customerId, so an install id alone can never produce a binding.
approved_rules_implemented.route: A refused claim is a 409 rather than a 201 carrying a quiet bound:false nobody reads, and the holder's identity is never in the response body.

sabotage_verification: A the holder's id returned to the second customer (the original line) -> DI-03, DI-12 red
B silent transfer restored -> DI-02, DI-04, DI-05, DI-12 red
C release skips the holder check -> DI-06 red
D release of an unbound install accepted -> DI-10 red
E handover linkage not recorded -> DI-08 red
F route answers 201 on a refused claim -> DI-12 red

still_open_and_not_claimed.notification_rotation: The rule asks for removal or rotation of the previous notification/session association. install_identity_links IS the only install-keyed association in this repository - there is no push-token or device-session table - so releasing it is the whole of that step today. When push tokens land they must be rotated on release, and that is recorded here rather than pretended.
still_open_and_not_claimed.customer_facing_release: releaseInstall is reachable from lib and from the staff funnel route. There is no customer-facing sign-out action wired to it; the customer app calling it on logout is app work.
